correctness.rationale: For any d>=3, convex base B with full-dimensional John ellipsoid normalized to unit (d-1)-ball, and any q in [0,1], the claimed ellipsoid with a^2=max(q,(d-1)/(d+1)) and axial radius=height b=min(1/2,1/((d+1)(1-q))) lies in the homothetic frustum: the Cauchy–Schwarz side-support maximum equals 1-(1-q)b, and 0<=z<=2b<=1. Lifting arbitrary John base support contacts xi to (sqrt(1-y^2)xi,y), plus bottom and when touching top poles, gives positive contact masses lambda, alpha, beta satisfying zero mean and covariance I_d/d. Independently verified exact fractions for d=3..15 at five q including cone/transition/prism; the general identities and John optimality theorem establish global unrestricted maximality for any base, not merely rotational candidates. Exact volume integration yields Fd=d a^(d-1)b/sum(q^j); the cone branch Fd=C/(1-q^d) increases and the top-contact branch increases by paired reciprocal powers, with endpoint Fd(1)=1/2.
residual_risks: The full theorem requires homothetic parallel sections with common center; not arbitrary prismatoids.
